{{Short description|In computability theory, the assignment of natural numbers to a set of objects}}
In [[computability theory]] a '''numbering''' is an assignment of [[natural number]]s to a [[Set (mathematics)|set]] of objects such as [[function (mathematics)|function]]s, [[rational number]]s, [[Graph (discrete mathematics)|graph]]s, or words in some [[formal language]]. A numbering can be used to transfer the idea of computability and related concepts, which are originally defined on the natural numbers using [[computable function]]s, to these different types of objects.

Common examples of numberings include [[Gödel numbering]]s in [[first-order logic]], the [[description number]]s that arise from [[universal Turing machine]]s and [[admissible numbering]]s of the set of partial computable functions.

== Definition and examples ==
A '''numbering''' of a set <math>S</math> is a [[surjective function|surjective]] [[partial function]] from <math>\mathbb{N}</math> to ''S'' ([[Yury Yershov|Ershov]] 1999:477). The value of a numbering <math>\nu</math> at a number ''i'' (if defined) is often written <math>\nu_i</math> instead of the usual <math>\nu(i)</math>.

Examples of numberings include:
* The set of all finite subsets of <math>\mathbb{N}</math> has a numbering <math>\gamma</math> , defined so that <math>\gamma(0) = \emptyset</math> and so that, for each finite nonempty set <math>A = \{a_0, \ldots, a_k\}</math>, <math>\gamma(n_A) = A</math> where <math>n_A = \sum_{i \leq k} 2^{a_i}</math> (Ershov 1999:477).  This numbering is an injection. 
* A fixed Gödel numbering <math>\varphi_i</math> of the computable partial functions can be used to define a numbering ''W'' of the [[computably enumerable set]]s, by letting by ''W''(''i'') be the domain of <math>\varphi_i</math>.  This numbering will be surjective (like all numberings) but not injective: there will be distinct numbers that map to the same computably enumerable set under ''W''.

== Types of numberings ==

A numbering is '''total''' if it is a total function. If the [[domain (function)|domain]] of a partial numbering is [[computably enumerable]] then there always exists an equivalent total numbering (equivalence of numberings is defined below).

A numbering ''&eta;'' is '''decidable''' if the set <math>\{ (x,y) : \eta(x) = \eta(y)\}</math> is a decidable set.

A numbering ''&eta;'' is '''single-valued''' if ''&eta;''(''x'') = ''&eta;''(''y'') if and only if ''x''=''y''; in other words if ''&eta;'' is an injective function. A single-valued numbering of the set of partial computable functions is called a [[Friedberg numbering]].

== Comparison of numberings ==

There is a [[preorder]] on the set of all numberings. Let <math>\nu_1: \mathbb{N} \rightharpoonup S</math> and <math>\nu_2: \mathbb{N} \rightharpoonup S</math> be two numberings. Then <math>\nu_1</math> is '''reducible''' to <math>\nu_2</math>, written <math>\nu_1 \le \nu_2</math>, 
if 
:<math>\exists f \in \mathbf{P}^{(1)} \, \forall i \in \mathrm{Domain}(\nu_1) : \nu_1(i) = \nu_2 \circ f(i).</math>
Where <math>\mathbf{P}^{(1)}</math> is the set of all partial computable functions <math>\mathbb N \to \mathbb N</math>.

If <math>\nu_1 \le \nu_2</math> and <math>\nu_1 \ge \nu_2</math> then  <math>\nu_1</math> is '''equivalent''' to <math>\nu_2</math>; this is written <math>\nu_1 \equiv \nu_2</math>.

== Computable numberings ==

When the objects of the set ''S'' being numbered are sufficiently "constructive", it is common to look at numberings that can be effectively decoded (Ershov 1999:486). For example, if ''S'' consists of computably enumerable sets, the numbering ''&eta;'' is '''computable''' if the set of pairs (''x'',''y'') where ''y'' &isin; ''&eta;''(''x'') is computably enumerable.  Similarly, a numbering ''g'' of partial functions is computable if the relation ''R''(''x'',''y'',''z'') = "[''g''(''x'')](''y'') = ''z''" is computably enumerable (Ershov 1999:487).

A computable numbering is called '''principal''' if every computable numbering of the same set is reducible to it. Both the set of all computably enumerable subsets of <math>\mathbb{N}</math> and the set of all partial computable functions have principal numberings (Ershov 1999:487). A principal numbering of the set of partial computably functions is known as an [[admissible numbering]] in the literature.
